content.title: About
content.content: Grapes are small, juicy, sweet berries that grow in clusters on the vines of Vitis vinifera and related species, cultivated for thousands of years. They come in green, red, purple, and black varieties, seeded and seedless. Grapes are eaten fresh, dried as raisins, and made into juice, wine, and vinegar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grapes are among the oldest cultivated fruits, with a history of at least several thousand years.
Raisins are dried grapes, and currants and sultanas are types of dried grapes.
Grapes are used to make wine, juice, jams, and vinegar.
Red and purple grapes contain resveratrol and other polyphenols, mostly in the skin.
Grapes do not ripen after being picked, so they are harvested when ripe.

items.title: Contains polyphenols
items.content: Grapes, especially red and purple ones, contain resveratrol and anthocyanins with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Provides vitamin K and vitamin C
items.content: These vitamins support blood clotting and the immune system.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Hydrating
items.content: Grapes are high in water and a refreshing snack.

items.title: Convenient
items.content: Grapes are portable and need no preparation.

items.title: Natural sugar content
items.content: Grapes contain natural sugars, so portions matter for people monitoring blood sugar.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole grapes are a choking hazard for young children and should be cut lengthwise.

items.title: Toxic to dogs
items.content: Grapes and raisins are toxic to dogs and can cause kidney damage, so keep them away from pets.

items.title: Pesticide residues and allergies
items.content: Wash grapes before eating. Allergy to grapes is uncommon but can occur.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grapes can be eaten fresh as a snack, added to fruit and chicken salads, frozen as a cool treat, or roasted. They can be pressed into juice or dried into raisins. Choose whole grapes over juice for more fiber.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unwashed grapes in the refrigerator in a breathable bag or container, where they usually keep for one to two weeks. Wash them just before eating. Remove any soft or moldy grapes. Grapes can also be frozen.
